sources.quote: Many counties in the Delta and Appalachian regions have held this designation for years
sources.searcher_note: Headline: Delta and Appalachian regions 'medically underserved' for decades. Names the Delta region, not specific counties or the 1978-89 cohort count; body text is thin.

sources.quote: 73 percent of HPSA-designated counties were still experiencing a physician shortage ten years after its designation.
sources.searcher_note: Reports the Health Affairs study (Nov 2023) that most HPSA counties stay shortage areas 10+ years. National pattern, no named counties or 1978-89 cohort.

sources.quote: Those HPSAs that were proposed for withdrawal because they no longer meet the HPSA criteria have retained their HPSA designation.
sources.searcher_note: GAO: HRSA did not remove HPSAs that no longer met criteria. Cuts against reading long-lived designations as proof of ongoing shortage (matches the lead's own watch-out).

sources.quote: many have not been reviewed since their creation in the 1970s and 1980s
sources.searcher_note: Think tank on stale shortage designations; this passage is about MUA/MUP designations, not primary-care HPSAs. Pattern only.

sources.quote: The town of Belzoni, Miss., has just four doctors serving all of Humphreys County and surrounding areas.
sources.searcher_note: Names Humphreys County's doctor shortage (one of the lead's severe examples), but says nothing about shortage-area designation age.

sources.quote: This county lost its hospital. Bringing it back is easier said than done
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff piece on Humphreys County having no hospital. WebFetch got HTTP 403 (bot wall), so quote is the headline only; body not read. About hospital loss, not designation age.

notes: No source found names the 143 still-designated 1978-89 primary-care HPSAs, or the 31 severe ones, or Jefferson/Copiah MS or Jim Hogg TX as long-running HPSAs. Coverage found is pattern: HPSA counties stay designated 10+ years (Health Affairs 2023 via TechTarget; the Health Affairs and PubMed pages themselves returned 403/captcha), GAO 2006 saying HRSA failed to drop outdated HPSAs, and Paragon 2024 on MUAs not reviewed since the 1970s-80s. WLBT 2021 says Delta counties have held the designation for decades but names no county. Mississippi Today 2026-07-16 page was blocked (403); only the headline is recorded. Only 7 queries run; stopped there to stay under the shared budget, since the entity-specific searches came back empty.
